title: Bash Shell Scripting
description: Bash reference covering quoting, parameters, arrays, tests, pipelines, functions, traps, files, processes, portability, security, debugging, and production-grade scripting.

subtopics.title: Options, Quoting & Expansion Order
subtopics.description: Quote parameter expansions by default. Use arrays for argument lists and understand that shell parsing happens before commands receive arguments.

callouts.title: Do Not Change IFS Globally by Habit
callouts.text: Quoting expansions and using arrays preserve argument boundaries. Set IFS locally for a specific read or split operation instead of changing it for the entire script.

callouts.title: Strict Mode Is Not Error Handling
callouts.text: set -e has contextual exceptions. Handle expected failures explicitly and test pipelines, conditions, subshells, and cleanup paths.

subtopics.title: Parameters, Defaults & Arrays
subtopics.description: Use parameter expansion for required/default values and indexed/associative arrays to preserve argument boundaries.

codeBlocks.code:
environment=${ENVIRONMENT:-dev}
: "${DATABASE_URL:?DATABASE_URL is required}"
files=("report one.csv" "report two.csv")
declare -A ports=([http]=80 [https]=443)
command -- "${files[@]}"

subtopics.title: [[ ]], Arithmetic, case & Loops
subtopics.description: Prefer [[ ]] in Bash for strings/patterns, (( )) for arithmetic, case for dispatch, and read loops that preserve whitespace.

codeBlocks.code:
if [[ -f $config && $environment == prod ]]; then load_config "$config"; fi
case $command in start|stop) run "$command" ;; *) usage >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
while IFS= read -r line; do process "$line"; done < "$input"

subtopics.title: Functions, Exit Status & Traps
subtopics.description: Functions return integer status, not rich values. Send data to stdout deliberately, diagnostics to stderr, and install cleanup traps early.

codeBlocks.code:
tmp_dir=$(mktemp -d)
cleanup() {
  local status=$?
  trap - EXIT
  rm -rf -- "$tmp_dir"
  exit "$status"
}
trap cleanup EXIT
trap 'exit 130' INT
trap 'exit 143' TERM
log() { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }

callouts.title: Keep Cleanup Idempotent
callouts.text: Signal handlers commonly exit and then trigger the EXIT trap. Register cleanup on EXIT once, or clear traps before exiting, so cleanup cannot recurse or run twice.

callouts.title: Validate Destructive Targets
callouts.text: Before rm/mv/chmod, reject empty, root, home, unresolved, and unexpected paths. Prefer explicit paths over globs.

subtopics.title: Pipelines, Subshells & Background Jobs
subtopics.description: Pipeline stages usually run in separate processes; pipefail surfaces earlier failures; capture PIDs and wait to own background work.

codeBlocks.code:
producer | transformer | consumer
printf '%s\n' "${PIPESTATUS[@]}"
worker_one & pid_one=$!
worker_two & pid_two=$!
wait "$pid_one"; wait "$pid_two"

subtopics.title: Files, find, NUL Delimiters & Portability
subtopics.description: Use NUL delimiters for arbitrary filenames, -- before path operands, and select Bash versus POSIX sh deliberately.

codeBlocks.code:
while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
  sha256sum -- "$file"
done < <(find "$root" -type f -print0)

callouts.title: Never Parse ls
callouts.text: Filenames may contain spaces, tabs, newlines, and leading dashes. Use globs, find -print0, or arrays.

subtopics.title: Tracing, ShellCheck & Tests
subtopics.description: Use bash -n for syntax, ShellCheck for static issues, controlled xtrace for debugging, and automated tests for edge-case inputs and failure paths.

codeBlocks.code:
bash -n script.sh
shellcheck script.sh
PS4='+${BASH_SOURCE}:${LINENO}:${FUNCNAME[0]}: ' bash -x script.sh

subtopics.title: Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Pin commands and formats, validate environment/input, avoid eval, preserve exit statuses, bound retries, and make reruns idempotent.

callouts.title: Production Checklist
callouts.text: Quote expansions, use arrays, validate paths, create secure temp files, trap cleanup, avoid secret xtrace, check dependencies, use timeouts, lint, test, and document Bash-only features.
